title: 17. I'm Sorry, Too
reviewMethod: English read-aloud translation compared with every original Korean page

pages.text: Hori had been pouting since morning. Hmph! Everyone dislikes me! He stamped his feet outside the Rainbow Class door. Somehow, it felt as though nobody liked him today.
Inside, Toto and Kongi were laughing and building with blocks. Hori quietly came closer, but nobody said, Come and join us! See? They won't play with me. Hori pressed his lips together.
Hori crouched alone on a cushion in the corner, with drooping shoulders and a bowed head. Toto, Bori, Kongi. They all dislike me. His eyes stung and filled with tears.
Then Hori remembered that morning. Toto, with a bandage on one knee, had waved happily. Hi, Hori! But Hori had been sulking and walked straight past. I should have asked, Toto, is your knee okay?

Then he remembered the playground yesterday. While running, he had bumped into Bori. Thump! But he had rushed away without saying sorry. Bori had fallen and looked startled. Bori must have been really surprised.
And then there was Kongi. When Kongi dropped a pile of acorns, Hori had pointed and laughed. Kongi's cheeks are so puffy! Kongi had looked down. I must have hurt Kongi's feelings.
Hori felt a pang inside. Oh! It wasn't that everyone disliked me. I had been unkind first. His sulky feelings began to fade, and sorry feelings filled his heart instead.
Then Toto, Bori, and Kongi ran over. Hori, why are you alone? Sorry we didn't notice you earlier. Come and play! The friends held out their hands first. Hori was surprised.

Hori found his courage. He stood up and held their hands. No, I'm sorry, too! I didn't ask about Toto's knee. I bumped into Bori without apologizing, and I teased Kongi. I'm really sorry! His tail stripes sparkled like a rainbow, and his heart felt brighter.
The friends hugged Hori. It's okay. We're friends again! In that big hug, everyone felt warm and burst into laughter. Sometimes it isn't dislike at all. Saying sorry can open our hearts again.
